messages.content: I need to start planning a San Diego weekend for my spouse and me. We can leave Denver Friday, October 23, and come back Monday, October 26. The anniversary dinner is Saturday at 6:30 p.m. in Point Loma, and everyone is gathering Sunday afternoon near Balboa Park.
I can compare flights and one-room hotel combinations around those two locations. Do you have a preferred Friday arrival window or a latest acceptable return to Denver on Monday?

Friday is flexible, but I would rather arrive by midafternoon so we are not spending the whole first evening in transit. Monday we should be home by about 8:00 p.m. Nonstop flights would be best if the price is reasonable.

For two adults, the useful nonstop patterns currently look like this: a 7:35 a.m. Denver departure arriving San Diego at 9:05 a.m. for about $708 round trip total; an 11:20 a.m. departure arriving at 12:50 p.m. for about $756 total; and a 2:10 p.m. departure arriving at 3:40 p.m. for about $684 total. Monday nonstop returns include 10:15 a.m.-1:40 p.m., 1:45-5:10 p.m., and 4:05-7:30 p.m. The lowest fare pairs with the 2:10 p.m. outbound and 4:05 p.m. return, but that Friday arrival leaves less daylight for checking in and settling down. These are current comparison fares and would need a live recheck before purchase.
The 11:20 Friday flight sounds better than either extreme. Which Monday flight is included in that $756?

The $756 total pairs the 11:20 a.m. Friday outbound with the 1:45 p.m. Monday return, both nonstop. You would land in Denver at 5:10 p.m. The 4:05 p.m. return raises the total to about $812, while the 10:15 a.m. return lowers it slightly to about $724.
Keep the 1:45 Monday return in the comparison. Now show me how the hotel locations work. I was thinking waterfront near the dinner, but Sunday and the airport may make downtown more sensible.

Two areas fit that tradeoff. A Shelter Island waterfront hotel is roughly 8-12 minutes from the Point Loma dinner, 12-18 minutes from the airport, and 18-25 minutes from Balboa Park in ordinary traffic. A Little Italy or north-downtown hotel is about 12-18 minutes from the dinner, 5-10 minutes from the airport, and 8-12 minutes from Balboa Park. Saturday evening traffic can add 10 minutes around Point Loma, while Sunday parking near Balboa Park can add time even when the drive itself is short.
Can you put actual hotels and totals against those areas? One room, two adults, Friday through Monday.

I found three representative refundable options for three nights. The waterfront option is Kona Kai Resort on Shelter Island: one king room, approximately $1,184 including estimated taxes and resort charges, with parking around $47 per night. In Little Italy, the Carte Hotel has one king at approximately $1,096 including estimated taxes and destination charges, with parking around $60 per night. The more central alternative is a king room at the Courtyard San Diego Downtown for about $914 including estimated taxes, with parking around $58 per night. Exact room terms and mandatory charges need confirmation on the booking page.
We will probably rent a car, so include parking. Also, the Courtyard sounds farther south than I want. Is there something between Little Italy and Balboa Park?

The Inn at the Park is the clearest location match. It is on the west side of Balboa Park, around 10-15 minutes from the airport, 15-20 minutes from Point Loma, and close enough to the Sunday gathering area that the exact address may be walkable or a short ride. A king studio is about $1,022 including estimated taxes for three nights. Valet parking is approximately $35 nightly, bringing the lodging-and-parking estimate to about $1,127.
How do the all-in estimates compare once parking is added to the other two?

Using three parking nights, the estimated totals are: Kona Kai about $1,325; Carte about $1,276; and Inn at the Park about $1,127. Those figures exclude the rental car itself and any incidental holds. Carte is the shortest airport trip, Kona Kai is easiest for Saturday's dinner, and Inn at the Park is strongest for Sunday's gathering while remaining workable for Point Loma.
Would staying on Shelter Island create any real problem for the Sunday gathering, or is it just a longer drive?

It is mainly a longer drive rather than a logistical problem. I would allow 30-35 minutes door to door on Sunday to account for the 18-25 minute drive plus finding parking or reaching the specific gathering point. From Inn at the Park, the same trip could be a few minutes by car and may avoid moving the rental car if the gathering is on the west side of the park. The exact Sunday address will decide how meaningful that advantage is.
The gathering is at a relative's building near Sixth Avenue and Laurel Street. Dinner is near Shelter Island Drive and Anchorage Lane.

That makes Inn at the Park especially convenient on Sunday: Sixth and Laurel is roughly a 10-15 minute walk, depending on the building entrance. Kona Kai is only a few minutes from the Saturday dinner address, while Carte is about 8-12 minutes by car from Sunday's location and roughly 15-20 minutes from the dinner. For the full weekend, Inn at the Park minimizes Sunday effort; Kona Kai gives you the waterfront setting and makes Saturday nearly effortless.
Let's drop the Carte. Between the other two, what would Friday and Monday look like with the 11:20 outbound and 1:45 return?

With the 11:20 a.m. Friday nonstop, arrival is 12:50 p.m. Allowing about 45-60 minutes to deplane and collect a rental car, you could reach Kona Kai around 2:00 p.m. or Inn at the Park around 2:10 p.m.; either may require luggage storage before standard check-in. On Monday, leaving Kona Kai around 11:15 a.m. or Inn at the Park around 11:25 a.m. should provide a reasonable cushion to return the car and check in for the 1:45 p.m. flight. Both hotels work cleanly with those flights.
And the combined flight plus hotel and parking totals for two adults?

Using the $756 flight total for two adults, Kona Kai comes to approximately $2,081 for flights, room, estimated mandatory hotel charges, and three nights of parking. Inn at the Park comes to approximately $1,883 on the same basis. The difference is about $198. Rental-car cost, fuel, meals, and refundable incidental deposits are not included.

I do like the waterfront, but nearly two hundred dollars plus the Sunday inconvenience is probably not worth it. Is the Inn room actually refundable, and does it have one bed rather than a sofa-bed arrangement?

The quoted Inn at the Park option is listed as a king studio with one king bed; the room may also have a sitting area, but the primary bed is not a sofa bed. The displayed rate is refundable without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local hotel time on October 20. After that, the stated penalty is one night's room and tax. I would verify both the room description and deadline again before booking because inventory and terms can change.
Good. Narrow it to the Inn at the Park and those midday nonstops, but do not book anything yet. What still needs checking?

The working combination is the Friday 11:20 a.m. Denver-San Diego nonstop, arriving 12:50 p.m.; the Monday 1:45 p.m. nonstop, arriving Denver at 5:10 p.m.; and one king studio at Inn at the Park for Friday, October 23 through Monday, October 26. The current combined estimate is about $1,883 for two passengers, three hotel nights, estimated mandatory charges, and three nights of valet parking. Before booking, recheck live flight times and fare rules, baggage and seat charges, the hotel's final tax-and-fee breakdown, the king-bed room description, the October 20 cancellation deadline, valet availability, and whether luggage can be held before Friday check-in and after Monday checkout. Nothing has been booked.
